activities.title: Three checks before you trust any AI answer
activities.intro: Run the three checks on your own inventory file. They take about 2 minutes and work on any formula, not just AI ones.

items: Check 2 rows by hand: use a calculator on row 2 and row 9.
Check the range: click E10 and read the formula bar. Does it cover all 8 items and not the TOTAL row?
Check against the total: add the parts another way and compare.
Sense check: does the answer make sense? An average bigger than the biggest item is a red flag.

blocks.prompt: Which range should the grand total in E10 cover?

help: Check the first and the last row: range errors usually hit the ends.
Our average Total Cost is ₱2,754.88. If an AI says ₱27,000, something is off.

activities.title: Be the supervisor: find the 3 mistakes
activities.intro: This AI answer is made up for practice, but every error in it happens in real life. Use the three checks to find what is wrong.

items: Read the four lines of the AI answer on the slide.
Check each formula's range and each fact against your inventory.
Pick the lines that are wrong, then say why.

blocks.prompt: Which lines of the AI answer are wrong? Pick all that apply.
options: 3. Your most expensive item is printer ink at ₱2,800.00.

blocks.prompt: What does =SUM(E2:E8) give on your inventory?
Line 4 uses a function that doesn't exist. Type the real formula that counts the items in A2:A9.
In one line each, why are the wrong lines wrong?

help: Click the cell and read the formula bar: does the range reach row 9?
Not sure a function exists? Type = and the first letters, and look at the list that pops up.

activities.title: Ask, paste, then run the three checks
activities.intro: Use an office-approved AI tool, or follow the Resource Person's screen. Share headers only, never real records.

items: Open an office-approved AI tool. Describe your app, headers and rows: A Item, B Unit, C Qty, D Unit Cost, E Total Cost, data in rows 2 to 9.
Ask for the AVERAGE of Total Cost, and the formula to count items above ₱1,000.
Paste both formulas into empty cells on your Jan sheet.
Run the 3 checks: 2 rows by hand, the range, the total.

blocks.prompt: What average Total Cost did you get?
How many items have a Total Cost above ₱1,000?
Write "verified" and what you checked, or the mistake you caught.

help: No AI tool at your desk? Suggest prompts in the chat and the Resource Person will test them on screen.
A different formula from the AI is fine if it gives the same answer. The point is the checking.
Seeing #NAME?? The AI used a function that doesn't exist or isn't in your app version. Tell it your exact app and version.

activities.title: Quick check: #NAME? from an AI formula

blocks.prompt: AI suggests =SUMVALUES(E2:E9). The cell shows #NAME?. What happened?
options: The function doesn't exist; the AI invented it
The numbers are stored as text

activities.title: Lab 3: Spreadsheet Tracking and Verification
activities.intro: Build a working tracker, then prove it's right. Choose one scenario: the default office supplies inventory (Item, Unit, Qty, Unit Cost, Total Cost, Reorder Level, with the 8 items from this module), a store's week of sales (Day, Item, Qty Sold, Price, Sales = Qty × Price), or a monthly budget (Category, Budget, Actual, Difference = Actual − Budget). Enter and format the data, use working formulas with SUM and AVERAGE, verify one AI-suggested formula, and add a titled chart. Save it as Lab3_Surname. This lab is worth 30% of the course grade.

items: Every column has a clear header in row 1. The data is tidy, with no blank rows.
At least one column is formatted as Currency (₱) or Date.
Totals use working formulas such as =C2*D2, filled down. No hard-typed results.
=SUM() and =AVERAGE() are used on the correct ranges, and the results are accurate.
A Pie, Bar or Line chart fits the data, uses the right range (no TOTAL row), and has a real title.
A short note (for example on a Notes sheet) says which AI formula you used, what you checked, and that it matched.
The file is saved as Lab3_Surname.

blocks.prompt: Paste your verification note: the AI formula, what you checked, and the result.

criteria.name: Chart (Pie, Bar or Line) with a real title

help: Type numbers as numbers: no ₱ sign or spaces typed in, or they become text.
Ask the AI with headers only. Never paste client data or personal records.
Two lines are enough for the note, for example: AI suggested =AVERAGE(E2:E9). Checked rows 2 and 9 by hand; totals match.
Save often with Ctrl + S. A brownout during a 4-hour lab is a real risk.
